# watchpoint_derived_metric_rule (Resource)

A derived metric rule: a span-derived metric (`source = "span"`) or a recording rule (`source = "metric"`) that emits an hourly series into the tenant's metric rollups, where dashboards, the metrics explorer and alert rules read it like any ingested metric. The emitted series is named by `metric_name`, not by `name`: the API forces it into the reserved `span.` or `rule.` namespace so it can never collide with an ingested metric. Only `enabled` can be changed in place; every other attribute replaces the rule. Requires the `derived_metric_rules` feature flag, and an API key with the `settings.manage` scope.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A span-derived metric: how many checkout spans, broken down by status and route.
# The emitted series is "span.checkout.errors" - reference metric_name, not name.
resource "watchpoint_derived_metric_rule" "checkout_errors" {
  name    = "span.checkout.errors"
  source  = "span"
  service = "checkout-api"

  labels = ["status", "http.route"]

  filters = {
    "http.request.method" = "POST"
  }
}

# A recording rule: fold an expensive series to one precomputed value per hour so
# a dashboard or an alert reads a single row instead of re-aggregating.
resource "watchpoint_derived_metric_rule" "checkout_p95" {
  name        = "rule.checkout.latency.p95"
  source      = "metric"
  metric      = "http.server.request.duration"
  aggregation = "p95"
}

output "checkout_error_metric" {
  value = watchpoint_derived_metric_rule.checkout_errors.metric_name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name to derive the emitted metric from. The API lower-cases it, replaces separators with `.` and prefixes it with `span.` or `rule.`; the result is `metric_name`. Write the fully qualified form (`span.checkout.errors`) to have the two match exactly. Changing it replaces the rule.

### Optional

- `aggregation` (String) Recording rules only, and REQUIRED for them: how the source series' hour is folded to one value. One of `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`, `p50`, `p95`, `p99`. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is evaluated. Defaults to `true`. Pausing a rule stops it at the next cycle and keeps the series it has already emitted; deleting the rule drops those buckets too. Resuming does NOT back-fill the paused hours beyond the evaluator's own floor.
- `filters` (Map of String) Span rules only: up to 5 span-attribute equality predicates, for example `{ "http.request.method" = "POST" }`. Changing them replaces the rule.
- `labels` (Set of String) Span rules only: up to 3 label keys to break the metric down by. `service`, `operation`, `status` come from the span's own columns; any other key is read from the span attributes and is refused when that key's distinct-value estimate is over the tenant's cardinality limit, because promoting it would create one series per value. Changing the set replaces the rule.
- `metric` (String) Recording rules only, and REQUIRED for them: the existing metric the rule reads. It may not itself be a recording rule (anything in the `rule.` namespace), which is what makes evaluation cycles impossible. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `operation` (String) Span rules only: an optional span name (operation) filter. Omit to match every operation in the service. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `service` (String) Span rules only, and REQUIRED for them: the single `service.name` to match. There is deliberately no all-services rule, because the service is what keeps the hourly scan an index range instead of the whole span firehose. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `source` (String) What the rule reads: `span`, `metric`. Defaults to `span`. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `value` (String) Span rules only: what is measured per matched span. `count` (one unit per span, the default), `duration` (the span duration in milliseconds), or `attr:<key>` for a numeric span attribute - a non-numeric value is skipped, not counted as zero. Ignored for a recording rule. Changing it replaces the rule.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Derived metric rule ID.
- `last_run_at` (String) When the evaluator last processed this rule (RFC 3339), if ever.
- `last_status` (String) Last failure reason (over the scan budget, an invalid filter, ...), or null when the last cycle succeeded.
- `metric_name` (String) The emitted metric name, in the reserved namespace for the source. This is what a dashboard widget or alert rule queries.
- `series_count` (Number) How many distinct label series the rule has emitted. Worth watching: each one is a billable metric series.
- `type` (String) The metric type the rule emits, derived by the API from the rule itself: `counter` for a span count, `histogram` for a measured span value, `gauge` for a recording rule.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID is the rule id.
terraform import watchpoint_derived_metric_rule.example dmr_001
```
